items.text: `quote` is a verbatim passage from the source, at most 50 words, where the claim and its `basis` are put forward.
`location` is a page number or, without pagination, section heading plus paragraph ordinal (e.g. "3.2, para 4");

claim.anchors.label: Anchors
claim.anchors.text: a list of 1 to N textual quotes, each `{quote, location}`:

items.text: the claim is based on data, experiments, interviews, or observation;
the claim is based on legislation, regulation and judicial decisions;
the claim is based on or summarizes previous findings from the scientific literature;
the claim is based on abstract/conceptual considerations.

claim.basis.label: Basis
claim.basis.text: always filled; what the source offers for the claim:

items.text: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code for a state, or `EU` for the European Union
the claim is explicitly not tied to any legal system or concerns law in general (the source presents it as jurisdiction-independent);
the claim does not say and the context does not settle it.

claim.claim_jurisdiction.label: Claim jurisdiction
claim.claim_jurisdiction.text: legal system(s) the claim is about or the jurisdiction(s) of the data the claim is based on. It can be more than one. Possible values:

items.text: the claim is about legislation, legal decisions, legal practices or regulators' behavior.
the claim is about computational technologies, systems or models.
the claim object does not fit the `law` or `technology` categories.

claim.claim_object.label: Claim object
claim.claim_object.text: what the claim is about. One of:

items.text: describes an aspect of the object or how it was/is handled.
proposes a prefered view of an aspect or concept of the object;
states how the object should be or should be handled;
is about future developments of the object and the ways it will or may be handled.

claim.claim_type.label: Claim type
claim.claim_type.text: how the object is addressed. One of:

claim.legal_reference.label: Legal reference
claim.legal_reference.text: instruments and provisions the claim is about, as written in the source, e.g. "AI Act, Art. 5"; "GDPR, Art. 22"; "Smith v Jones [2023] EWHC 1"; empty when none.

claim.node.label: Claim
claim.node.text: A claim is a central thesis or hypothesis that a paper advances as part of its contribution, especially when supported through arguments or empirical data.

claim.statement.label: Statement
claim.statement.text: the proposition itself, one per claim. Where one claim ends and the next begins is decided by the one-contention test in the `extract-claims` skill.

claim.temporal_reference.label: Temporal reference
claim.temporal_reference.text: date or period of the legal or factual state the claim describes, when stated; otherwise `as_of_publication`.

concept.definition.label: Concept definition
concept.definition.text: brief definition of the concept as understood within the corpus domain; the definition is inferred and continuously refined according to connected extracted claims. Each refinement appends an entry to `wiki/log.md` giving the concept id, the run id, and the replaced definition verbatim;

concept.node.label: Concept
concept.node.text: A concept is a notion that claims are about. A notion that nearly every paper in the corpus would trigger discriminates nothing, and is not a concept.

items.text: given in advance, listed in the grid below;
created during extraction (`map-concepts`);
a candidate promoted (`map-concepts`).

dataset.description.label: Description
dataset.description.text: quantitative and qualitative features of dataset: the type of data (e.g judgments, statutes, contracts, exam questions, synthetic etc.), annotation method, if present; size;

dataset.introduced_by.label: Introduced by
dataset.introduced_by.text: source id, when the dataset is introduced in the corpus; otherwise `external`.

dataset.jurisdiction.label: Jurisdiction
dataset.jurisdiction.text: legal system(s) the texts come from; jurisdiction codes in `schema/claim.md`.

dataset.language.label: Language
dataset.language.text: ISO 639-1 codes of the texts in the dataset.

dataset.name.label: Name
dataset.name.text: the dataset's name as the source gives it.

dataset.node.label: Dataset
dataset.node.text: One node per dataset, benchmark, or corpus a claim rests on. A dataset a paper merely mentions gets no node: if no claim rests on it, the graph has nothing to say about it.

sub: this paper cites the other where it makes the new claim; or
the other paper's claim carries the citation to this paper in its anchor quotes — by name, or by the marker the register prints for that paper. Read its claim records only, never its text.
items.text: when a CITES edge drafted at step 5 joins the two papers and the citation is on this point:
otherwise.

edge.grounding.label: Grounding
edge.grounding.verbatim:
- **`extracted`** when a CITES edge drafted at step 5 joins the two papers and the citation is on this point:
  - this paper cites the other where it makes the new claim; or
  - the other paper's claim carries the citation to this paper in its anchor quotes — by name, or by the marker the register prints for that paper. Read its claim records only, never its text.
- **`inferred`** otherwise.

edge.note.label: Relation Note
edge.note.text: one sentence saying why the edge holds; on `extracted` SUPPORTS and ATTACKS, naming the citation that grounds it. On the three claim-to-claim types only.

items.text: one claim gives reasons or evidence for another claim
one claim denies or gives reasons against another claim
two claims from different sources assert the same proposition

edge.relation_type.label: Relation type
edge.relation_type.text: one of the four types below.

skill.extract_claims.modality.label: Strength and modality
skill.extract_claims.modality.text:
Keep the modality of the statement as expressed in the source.
If the source says "may", write "may". Never turn "suggests" into "shows", or "should" into "must" and so on.

skill.extract_claims.standalone.label: Claim understood on its own
skill.extract_claims.standalone.text:
Someone who has not read the paper must understand it.

Cut every reference to the document. No "this work", no "the authors", no "as shown above".
